items.content_text:
arXiv:2607.21640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fix an integer $r\ge 2$ and a finite simple $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with at least one edge and no isolated vertices. An $n$-vertex $r$-graph is $\epsilon$-far from being $F$-free if at least $\epsilon n^r$ edges must be deleted to destroy every copy of $F$. A finite $r$-graph $H$ is $F$-abundant if there are constants $c,C>0$ such that every sufficiently large $\epsilon$-far host contains at least $c\epsilon^C n^{v(H)}$ labelled copies of $H$.
